text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The average eight percent rise in the 1996 net profit of Dutch listed companies contrasts sharply with the 33 pct rise in the AEX stock market index. (p1)
- Computer Company seeks bourse launch in order to reduce dependence on its financers. (p1)
- Banks, responding to demands from corporate customers, plan to speed up launch of electronic payment in euros. (p1)
- Bank insurer ING buys U.S. stock and insurance broker Vestax Securities. (p13) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet is close to an agreement on tax relief for fuel-efficient cars. (p1)
- Milk-based desserts company Mona plans to slash jobs to cut costs and stay competitive, even though it is profitable. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Israel has blocked the return of some hundred Palestinian refugees who were not allowed to settle in the Netherlands. (p1)
- Schiphol airport wants substantial government subsidy for a new airport to be built on land reclaimed from the sea. (p27)
- Japan's office automation and camera company Ricoh selects Schiphol as its European distribution centre. (p27) TROUW
- The Dutch are not as highly educated as government statistics suggest. (p1) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Port of Rotterdam port seeks to get a firmer grip on fraud. (p5)
